# MikroTik RouterOS — GUI ↔ CLI ↔ SNMP Mapping

Per [`gui-cli-snmp-unification.md`](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md): the CLI column is the literal command line a human would type, echoed verbatim into the terminal. Two structural notes carried over from [overview.md](overview.md) apply to every row below:

1. **No mode/context to enter or exit.** Every CLI command below is a complete, self-contained line — there is no "enter interface context, then issue bare commands" sequence the way Cisco/Arista/Huawei/Aruba require. SignalScope's session tracker does not need a "current mode" concept for RouterOS.
2. **No save step, ever.** Every command below takes effect and is durably persisted the instant it runs. There is no row for "persist configuration" in this table because no such action exists on this platform — see the dedicated note at the bottom instead.

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `/interface enable ether1` | **None.** No RouterOS documentation or `MIKROTIK-MIB` object confirms `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` as SET-able on this platform (see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md) — the entire MIB has only 3 read-write objects, none of them interface admin state). | `/interface print` (`R`/`X` flag columns) or `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` GET | **CLI-only.** Do not offer an SNMP fallback for this action on MikroTik — this is the one vendor in this project where even the near-universal `ifAdminStatus` baseline write is unconfirmed/likely absent. |
| Disable port | `/interface disable ether1` | Same as above — none confirmed. | Same as above | **CLI-only.** |
| Set port comment/description | `/interface set ether1 comment="uplink to core-sw1"` | Not confirmed (`ifAlias` write not documented for RouterOS — see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)). | `/interface print detail` or `IF-MIB::ifAlias` GET | **CLI-only**, pending live-device verification. |
| Set access port PVID | `/interface bridge port set [find interface=ether2] pvid=20` | Not confirmed. No RouterOS-documented SNMP path for bridge/VLAN membership; `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` write support not confirmed on this platform. | `/interface bridge port print detail` or `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid` GET | **CLI-only.** |
| Add bridge-VLAN entry (tagged/untagged membership) | `/interface bridge vlan add bridge=bridge1 tagged=ether1 untagged=ether2 vlan-ids=20` | Not confirmed. | `/interface bridge vlan print` | **CLI-only.** |
| Enable VLAN filtering on the bridge | `/interface bridge set bridge1 vlan-filtering=yes` | Not confirmed. | `/interface bridge print detail` | **CLI-only.** MikroTik's own guidance recommends configuring ports/VLAN table first and doing this from a session that can't be locked out (console/OOB), which SignalScope's GUI should surface as a warning before firing this specific action. |
| Set spanning-tree protocol mode | `/interface bridge set bridge1 protocol-mode=rstp` | Not confirmed — no MIB object in `MIKROTIK-MIB` and standard `BRIDGE-MIB` STP objects are read-only baseline. | `/interface bridge monitor bridge1` | **CLI-only.** |
| Create LACP bond | `/interface bonding add name=bond1 slaves=ether1,ether2 mode=802.3ad lacp-rate=1sec` | Not confirmed. | `/interface bonding monitor bond1` | **CLI-only**, consistent with every other vendor in this project — LACP membership has no confirmed SNMP write path anywhere in [comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md](../../comparison/snmp-write-support-matrix.md). |
| Configure bridge port isolation (`horizon`) | `/interface bridge port set [find interface=ether2] horizon=1` | Not confirmed. | `/interface bridge port print detail` | **CLI-only.** |
| Reboot the device | *(no direct CLI equivalent needed — this is the one action where SNMP is actually the more natural path)* `/system reboot` (CLI form, if issuing from a live session) | **`MIKROTIK-MIB::mtxrSystemReboot`, SET to any non-zero value** (`1.3.6.1.4.1.14988.1.1.7.1.0`) — **confirmed read-write** | N/A (device restarts) | **Genuine, confirmed SNMP write path** — one of only three writable objects in the entire enterprise MIB. Unusual among all vendor mapping files in this project in that the SNMP path is *not* a fallback-of-last-resort here; it's a legitimately simple one-object SET for an action that has no config-context prerequisites. |
| Cut USB port power (for N seconds) | `/system routerboard usb power-reset` (exact CLI form not independently confirmed this session — verify against target RouterOS release) | **`MIKROTIK-MIB::mtxrUSBPowerReset`, SET to desired seconds** (`1.3.6.1.4.1.14988.1.1.7.2.0`) — **confirmed read-write** | N/A | Confirmed SNMP write path; niche action (relevant mainly to routers with USB-powered peripherals, less so pure switch hardware). |
| Run a pre-staged script | `/system script run <script-name>` | **`MIKROTIK-MIB::mtxrScriptRunCmd`, SET to non-zero on the target script's table row** (indexed under `mtxrScriptTable`) — **confirmed read-write** | `/system script print` (to confirm the script ran, or check its effects via the relevant `show`/`print` for whatever the script did) | Confirmed SNMP write path, but only executes **administrator-predefined** RouterOS script logic — not a general mechanism for SignalScope to push arbitrary ad-hoc commands via SNMP. If a device has a script named e.g. `signalscope-safe-vlan-toggle` pre-staged by an operator, this becomes a legitimate SNMP-triggerable action; SignalScope should not assume such scripts exist by default. |
| Set system identity fields | `/system identity set name=<hostname>` (RouterOS-specific; distinct from SNMP `sysName`) | `SNMPv2-MIB::sysName`/`sysContact`/`sysLocation` — standard MIB-II objects, writable per usual semantics on any vendor | `/system identity print` or `SNMPv2-MIB::sysName` GET | Standard baseline write, not RouterOS-specific — included for completeness since it's genuinely one of the few working SNMP writes on this platform. |
| Enable the SNMP agent | `/snmp set enabled=yes` | N/A — configuring the SNMP agent itself cannot be done via SNMP (same chicken-and-egg limitation as every vendor in this project). | `/snmp print` | CLI-only by necessity. |
| Add an SNMP community | `/snmp community add name=ro-community address=10.0.0.0/24 read-access=yes` | N/A, same reasoning. | `/snmp community print detail` | CLI-only by necessity. |

## Backup/export — not a "save" action, included for completeness

Per [overview.md](overview.md), these are **not** prerequisites for any change above to take effect or survive reboot — they're portability/audit mechanisms SignalScope's config-drift-detection tier (see [connectivity-methods.md](../../00-architecture/connectivity-methods.md)) would use, distinct from every other vendor's "Save" GUI affordance:

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create a config backup snapshot | `/system backup save name=<file>` | None confirmed | Binary snapshot, not human-diffable. |
| Export config as replayable script | `/export file=<file>` | None confirmed | Human-readable `.rsc` text — the practical "show running-config" analogue for diffing. |

## Summary for SignalScope's capability matrix

MikroTik is, alongside Juniper, one of the two vendors in this project with essentially **no confirmed SNMP write path for switch configuration** (port state, VLAN, STP, LACP) — every one of those actions is CLI-only. Unlike Juniper (whose restriction stems from the candidate-config/commit model making SNMP structurally awkward even where objects exist), MikroTik's restriction is a deliberate vendor design choice: RouterOS's own documentation states plainly that "SNMP write access is only available for selected OIDs," and the entire `MIKROTIK-MIB` module has exactly three read-write objects, none of them configuration-related (reboot, USB power-reset, script-run trigger). SignalScope's GUI should treat MikroTik as functionally CLI/API-only for all configuration actions, with SNMP reserved for telemetry polling (where MikroTik's `mtxrHealth`/`mtxrInterfaceStats`/`mtxrPOE` groups are unusually rich, per [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)) and the narrow set of operational triggers above.
